title: Cross Sections and Solids of Revolution
seo_title: Geometry Cross Sections and Solids of Revolution Worksheets (TEKS G.10A)
short_title: Cross Sections and Solids of Revolution
standard_text: G.10A identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones, and spheres and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional shapes
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.10A: cross sections of prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones and spheres, and solids of revolution. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Slices parallel to the base match the base.
key_sub: A right triangle rotated about a leg makes a cone.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A cross section is the flat shape you get when you slice a solid.
  • Slices parallel to the base of a prism or cylinder match the base.
  • Any slice of a sphere is a circle. A cone sliced parallel to the base gives a circle; through the vertex, a triangle.
  • Rotating a rectangle about a side makes a cylinder; a right triangle about a leg makes a cone; a semicircle about its diameter makes a sphere.

Examples

Example

Rotate a right triangle about a leg

the leg is the axis

Answer: a cone

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Every slice of a cube is a squareSlanted slices can be rectangles, triangles or hexagons.
Mixing up slices of a coneParallel to the base: a circle.
Rotating about the wrong sideThe axis side becomes the height.

faq.a: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones, and spheres and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional shapes.

faq.q: Can a slice of a cube be a hexagon?
faq.a: Yes, with the right slanted cut.

faq.q: What solid does a circle rotated about a diameter make?
What is a cross section of a cylinder cut vertically through the axis?

sets.title: Cross sections of prisms and pyramids

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A cube is cut by a plane parallel to one face.
c: Rectangle that is not a square
items.e: Every slice parallel to a face is a copy of that face. Square.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A cube is cut by a plane through two opposite edges (diagonally through the cube).
c: Rectangle that is not a square
items.e: The cut goes along an edge and the diagonal of two faces, so it is longer one way than the other. Rectangle that is not a square.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A cube is cut by a plane through three vertices that are each next to the same corner.
items.e: Each side of the slice is a face diagonal, and all face diagonals are equal. Equilateral triangle.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A cube is cut by a plane through the midpoints of six of its edges, perpendicular to a long diagonal.
items.e: The slice crosses all six faces, and each side is the same length. Regular hexagon.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A rectangular prism is cut by a plane parallel to its base.
items.e: Slices parallel to the base are copies of the base. Rectangle.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A triangular prism is cut by a plane parallel to its triangular bases.
items.e: Slices parallel to the base are copies of the base. Triangle.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A triangular prism is cut by a plane perpendicular to its bases, through two lateral edges' midpoints parallel to a lateral face.
items.e: A vertical slice of a prism runs the full height, with straight parallel sides. Rectangle.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A square pyramid is cut by a plane parallel to its base.
c: Rectangle that is not a square
items.e: A slice parallel to the base is a smaller copy of the base. Square.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A square pyramid is cut by a vertical plane through its apex and the midpoints of two opposite base edges.
items.e: The slice goes through the apex down to the base, so it is a triangle with two equal slanted sides. Isosceles triangle.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A square pyramid is cut by a vertical plane that does not pass through the apex but is parallel to a base edge.
items.e: The slice is cut off below the apex, so the top edge is shorter than the bottom edge. Trapezoid.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A hexagonal prism is cut by a plane parallel to its bases.
items.e: Slices parallel to the base are copies of the base. Hexagon.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A pentagonal pyramid is cut by a plane parallel to its base.
items.e: A slice parallel to the base is a smaller copy of the base. Pentagon.

items.q: Which cross section is NOT possible for a cube?
items.e: A cube has only flat faces and straight edges, so a slice can never be curved. Circle.

items.q: Which cross section is NOT possible for a square pyramid?
items.e: A square pyramid has only five faces, so a slice can have at most five sides. Hexagon.

items.q: How many sides can a cross section of a cube have at most?
items.e: A plane can cross each of the 6 faces at most once, so at most 6 sides. 6.

items.q: A rectangular prism is cut by a plane perpendicular to its base. What shape is the cross section?
items.e: A vertical slice of a box has straight vertical sides and a straight top and bottom. Rectangle.

items.q: A cube with edges of 6 cm is cut parallel to one face. What is the area of the cross section?
items.e: The slice is a 6 cm by 6 cm square. 36 square centimeters.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 4 by 5 by 9 (height 9). What is the area of a cross section parallel to the base?
items.e: The slice is a copy of the 4 by 5 base: 4 × 5 = 20. 20.

items.q: A triangular prism has a right-triangle base with legs 6 and 8. What is the area of a cross section parallel to the base?
items.e: The slice is a copy of the base: ½ × 6 × 8 = 24. 24.

items.q: A cube is cut through four of its vertices, two on the top face and two on the bottom face, along diagonals of opposite faces. What shape is formed?
c: Rectangle that is not a square
Rhombus that is not a square
items.e: Its sides are an edge and a face diagonal, which are different lengths. Rectangle that is not a square.

sets.title: Cross sections of cylinders, cones and spheres

items.q: Which solid has circles for all of its horizontal cross sections, all the same size?
items.e: Picture slicing the solid. Cylinder.

items.q: Which solid has horizontal cross sections that are squares, all the same size?
items.e: Picture slicing the solid. Square prism.

items.q: Which solid has a circle as every cross section, no matter how it is cut?
items.e: Picture slicing the solid. Sphere.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A cone is cut by a vertical plane through its apex and the center of its base.
items.e: The slice has the two slant heights as equal sides and the diameter as the base. Isosceles triangle.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A cylinder is cut by a tilted plane that does not touch the bases.
items.e: A tilted slice through the curved side stretches the circle into an oval. Ellipse (an oval).

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base.
c: Ellipse that is not a circle
items.e: A slice parallel to the base is a smaller circle. Circle.

items.q: Which solid has a circle as its cross section parallel to the base and a triangle as its vertical cross section through the top?
items.e: Picture slicing the solid. Cone.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A cylinder is cut by a vertical plane through its axis.
items.e: The slice is as wide as the diameter and as tall as the cylinder. Rectangle.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A sphere is cut by any plane that passes through it.
c: Ellipse that is not a circle
items.e: Every slice of a sphere is a circle. Through the center it is a great circle. Circle.

items.q: Which solid has a square as its horizontal cross section and a triangle as its vertical cross section through the top?
items.e: Picture slicing the solid. Square pyramid.

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A sphere is cut by a plane through its center.
c: An ellipse that is not a circle
The largest possible circle (a great circle)
items.e: The slice through the center has the same radius as the sphere. The largest possible circle (a great circle).

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A cone is cut by a tilted plane that crosses only the curved surface.
items.e: Tilting the slice stretches the circle into an ellipse. Ellipse (an oval).

items.q: What shape is the cross section? A cylinder is cut by a plane parallel to its bases.
c: Ellipse that is not a circle
items.e: Each horizontal slice is a copy of the circular base. Circle.

items.q: A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 3 cm. Find the area of the vertical cross section through its axis.
items.e: The slice is a rectangle as wide as the diameter (6) and as tall as the cylinder (3): 18 square centimeters.

items.q: A sphere has radius 10 cm. A plane cuts it 6 cm from the center. Find the area of the cross section in terms of π.
items.e: The slice is a circle. Its radius, the distance 6 and the sphere's radius 10 form a right triangle: r² = 10² − 6² = 64. Area = 64π square centimeters.

items.q: A sphere has radius 17 cm. A plane cuts it 8 cm from the center. Find the area of the cross section in terms of π.
items.e: The slice is a circle. Its radius, the distance 8 and the sphere's radius 17 form a right triangle: r² = 17² − 8² = 225. Area = 225π square centimeters.

items.q: A square pyramid has base edges of 10 ft. A cross section parallel to the base is taken half of the way down from the apex. Find its area.
items.e: The slice is a square whose side is half of 10, which is 5 ft. Area = 5² = 25 ft².

items.q: A cone has base radius 4 in. and height 14 in. It is cut parallel to the base halfway up. Find the area of the cross section in terms of π.
items.e: Halfway up, the slice is a circle with half the radius: 2. Area = π × 2² = 4π in.².

items.q: A cylinder has radius 8 cm and height 13 cm. Find the area of the vertical cross section through its axis.
items.e: The slice is a rectangle as wide as the diameter (16) and as tall as the cylinder (13): 208 square centimeters.

items.q: A square pyramid has base edges of 8 ft. A cross section parallel to the base is taken half of the way down from the apex. Find its area.
items.e: The slice is a square whose side is half of 8, which is 4 ft. Area = 4² = 16 ft².

items.q: A 7 cm by 3 cm rectangle is rotated about its 7 cm side. What solid is formed, and what are its dimensions?
c: A cone with radius 3 cm and height 7 cm
A cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 7 cm
A cylinder with radius 1.5 cm and height 7 cm
A cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 3 cm
items.e: The side it turns around becomes the axis (the height). The other side sweeps out the radius. A cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 7 cm.

items.q: A 5 by 8 rectangle is rotated about its side of length 8. Which shape is the vertical cross section of the solid through its axis?
items.e: The solid is a cylinder with radius 5 and height 8. A slice through the axis is 10 wide (the diameter) and 8 tall. A 10 by 8 rectangle.

items.q: A 6 by 4 rectangle is rotated about its side of length 4. Which shape is the vertical cross section of the solid through its axis?
items.e: The solid is a cylinder with radius 6 and height 4. A slice through the axis is 12 wide (the diameter) and 4 tall. A 12 by 4 rectangle.

items.e: The circle sweeps around the line and leaves a hole in the middle. A torus (a donut shape).

sets.title: Volume of a solid of revolution

items.q: A right triangle with legs 2 in. and 6 in. is rotated about the 2 in. leg. Find the volume in terms of π.
items.e: The solid is a cone with radius 6 and height 2: ⅓ × π × 6² × 2 = 24π in.³.
